title: You’re not lost… you’re hiding.
paragraphs:
And deep down—
you know exactly where.

Not screaming.
Not condemning.
But calling.
Here’s the tension most people never resolve:

If God knows everything…
why does He ask questions?

Why walk into the garden
like He didn’t already see the leaves stitched together…
the shaking hands…
the guilty eyes?
Because this was never about geography.
Adam wasn’t just behind a tree.
He was buried under something heavier:

The kind that makes you avoid prayer.
The kind that makes you scroll instead of kneel.
The kind that whispers,
“Don’t let God see this version of you.”

And suddenly, intimacy with God
turns into distance from God.
Genesis records it with chilling honesty:
“But the Lord God called to the man, ‘Where are you?’” (Genesis 3:9)
“I heard you in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid.” (Genesis 3:10)
I was afraid… so I hid.

Sin enters.
Shame follows.
Hiding begins.
And we’ve been doing it ever since.
We hide behind filtered lives and unfiltered guilt.
But here’s the revelation that should shake you:

God didn’t ask,
“What did you do?”

Because before God addresses your sin…
He addresses your separation.
This is not a courtroom moment.
God walked toward the one who sinned.
And this is where everything shifts.

Because some scholars interpret this moment as the first picture of the Gospel—
God initiating restoration before man even understands repentance.
You didn’t go looking for God.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

Not when you cleaned yourself up.
Not when you fixed your habits.
Not when you became “worthy.”
And here’s where the story pierces deeper.
Adam hid in a tree line…
The first Adam used trees to hide from God.
The last Adam—Jesus Christ—used a tree (the cross) to bring you back to God.
“He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness.”
Jesus didn’t just carry your sin.
The shame that made Adam cover himself.
The shame that makes you avoid eye contact with heaven.
The shame you think disqualifies you.

If you keep hiding…
you will never experience what He died to give.
Grace is not found in hiding.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.”
God is not asking you for perfection.
Are you carrying something no one else knows?
Let me say this with love, but without softness:
You can sit in church and still be hiding.
You can post verses and still be hiding.
You can say “God is good” and still be hiding.
But His voice cuts through all of it.
Not to expose you for destruction…
But to invite you into redemption.
Because the same God who asked Adam that question…
Is the same God who sent His Son to answer it.
Jesus didn’t come to shame you.
“For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”
So if you feel exposed right now…
Step out from behind the tree.
And when you come out of hiding…
You’ll realize something that will break you—in the best way:
God wasn’t chasing you to punish you.
He was pursuing you to restore you.
And if this stirred something deep inside you…
